[[File:Michinoomi no Mikoto following a crow to the enemy's lair LACMA M.2000.105.97.jpg|thumb|Illustration of Michinoomi no Mikoto in ''Dai Nippon Meishōkan'' by {{ill|Tsukioka Yoshitoshi|en|Tsukioka Yoshitoshi|qid=Q467337|lt=Tsukioka Yoshitoshi|1=Tsukioka Yoshitoshi}}]]

'''Michinoomi no Mikoto''' (道臣命) is a legendary figure from ancient {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}. Initially named '''Hinoomi no Mikoto''' (日臣命), he was a descendant of {{ill|Amenooshihi no Mikoto|ja|天忍日命|1=Ama-no-Oshihi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenooshihi no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ama-no-Oshihi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシヒ}} and the ancestor of the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|en|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|qid=Q17227938|lt=Ōtomo clan|1=Ōtomo clan (ancient)}}. He served as a vanguard in {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu|1=Emperor Jimmu}}’s eastern campaign and later as a palace guard upon Emperor Jimmu’s accession.

== Achievements ==

During [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]], Michinoomi led the {{ill|Kumebe|ja|久米部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumebe}} warriors, guided by the divine {{ill|Yatagarasu|en|Yatagarasu|qid=Q745463|lt=Yatagarasu|1=Yatagarasu}}, to open a route from {{ill|Kumano region|en|Kumano region|qid=Q6443450|lt=Kumano|1=Kumano region}} to Uda (modern {{ill|Uda|ja|宇陀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uda|1=Uda|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11449912}}). For his accomplishments, Emperor Jimmu bestowed upon him the name "Michinoomi."

When {{ill|Eukashi|ja|兄猾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eukashi}} (Eukashi no Kami) attempted to ensnare Emperor Jimmu in a trap called "Oshi," Michinoomi confronted him, declaring, "Enter the house you built for yourself." With sword and bow ready, he forced Eukashi into his trap, where Eukashi perished. Michinoomi then dismembered Eukashi’s body, and the site became known as ''Chi-no-Hara'' (Blood Field) in Uda.

After the defeat of the {{ill|Yasotakeru|lt=Yasotakeru|lt=Eighty Bandit Chiefs|ja|八十梟帥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eighty Bandit Chiefs}} at Kunimi-dake, Michinoomi was tasked with eradicating their remnants. He constructed a grand chamber in the village of Osaka and lured the bandits to a banquet. At the height of the feast, he signaled his troops with a {{ill|Kumebushi|ja|久米節|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumebushi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} war song, and they drew their swords to annihilate the enemy.

Earlier, Michinoomi had been appointed by Emperor Jimmu to serve as a priest for the worship of {{ill|Takamimusubi|ja|高皇産霊尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamimusubi|qid=Q125400}}, earning the honorary title ''Izuhime'' (厳媛). Despite being male, this title reflects an ancient tradition of women officiating rituals.

Upon Emperor Jimmu’s enthronement, Michinoomi performed ceremonial songs and rituals to purify negative energies. In recognition of his service, he was granted a residence in ''Tsukisaka'' (present-day Kashihara, Nara Prefecture).
